subject.title: fix(acpx): drain leased descendants when turns are aborted

question: After survivor propagation is fixed, should ACPX cancellation always close the reusable live runtime and should any unverifiable stale lease block ACPX startup?
rationale: Upstream ACPX intentionally distinguishes cooperative cancel from close, while this PR trades session reuse and startup availability for stronger containment; that permanent security and recovery boundary requires owner intent.

options.title: Adopt fail-closed containment
options.body: Fix survivor propagation and require cancellation or startup to fail whenever ACPX-owned cleanup cannot be verified.

options.title: Preserve compatibility by default
options.body: Keep cooperative cancellation and startup availability as the default while adding an explicit strict containment policy with proof for both modes.

options.title: Narrow the patch
options.body: Land identity-safe survivor detection and truthful abort reporting while deferring runtime eviction and startup blocking.

recommendation.title: Adopt fail-closed containment
recommendation.body: Fix survivor propagation and require cancellation or startup to fail whenever ACPX-owned cleanup cannot be verified.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest combined current OpenClaw path and upstream ACPX runtime ownership history for the containment-policy choice.
